title: Why people hate journalists: Managing PR pitch overload on your Mac
metaTitle: Why people hate journalists: PR pitch management guide for Mac users
description: Journalists often feel overwhelmed by irrelevant PR pitches. Learn how to manage the noise and reclaim your inbox on macOS.
intro: The idea that people hate journalists often stems from the friction between newsrooms and PR professionals. You spend your day fighting a tide of irrelevant pitches that clutter your inbox and stall your actual reporting work.
tldr: Most PR pitches are irrelevant, with 88% of journalists deleting them immediately.
The core issue is a volume-based approach to pitching that ignores your specific beat.
You can reduce the noise by using filters, better organization, and clear boundaries.
Lazur helps you process communication faster by summarizing long threads and managing your daily tasks.

blocks.text: The reality of PR pitch overload

You likely feel the weight of a full inbox every morning. The industry standard for PR pitching is broken. Most firms use automated software to blast thousands of journalists at once. This creates a massive relevance gap. You are left to act as a human filter for content that was never meant for you.
Why this happens in modern newsrooms

Shrinking newsrooms mean you wear more hats than ever before. You are the researcher, the writer, and the editor. When a PR professional sends a template email, they are asking you to perform free labor. You have to verify the facts, check the source, and decide if it fits your publication. This is why you feel the pressure to block contacts or delete emails without opening them.
Fixing the PR noise without new software

items: Create specific filters in Gmail or Outlook to move emails with keywords like 'press release' or 'exclusive' to a side folder.
Use a dedicated email address for non-essential communications so your primary inbox remains clean.
Set clear expectations in your social media bios regarding how you prefer to be pitched.
Block repeat offenders who ignore your beat focus after three attempts.
Use the built-in search features in your mail app to find specific sources rather than relying on incoming pitches.

blocks.text: If you are struggling to keep up with your email, use the ⌘ + F shortcut to quickly find specific names or keywords in your inbox threads.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you manage your day

Lazur is a voice assistant that helps you move through your digital workspace. You do not need to click through dozens of tabs. When you hold ⌥ ⌘, you can ask about the content on your screen. Lazur can summarize an email or help you draft a quick response.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with my newsroom's email?
faq.answer: Lazur works in any app on your Mac. It reads the screen content when you hold the shortcut, so it works with Gmail, Outlook, or any other web-based mail client.

faq.question: Can Lazur automatically delete my PR emails?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate your apps for you. It can guide you through setting up your own email filters, but it will not perform the action on its own.

costs.title: Lost time
costs.text: Every irrelevant pitch is a distraction that pulls you away from your actual reporting and writing.

costs.title: Mental fatigue
costs.text: Constant context switching between pitches and real work contributes to burnout and reduces your creative output.

causes.title: Volume-based metrics
causes.text: PR firms often measure success by how many emails they send, leading to mass outreach that ignores your beat.

causes.title: Lack of personalization
causes.text: Template-based emails are easy to produce but rarely contain the specific information you need for a story.

fixes.title: The filter method
fixes.text: Use your mail app's rules to automatically move incoming pitches to a folder you check only once a day.

fixes.title: Public boundaries
fixes.text: Explicitly state your preferred pitching method in your professional profiles to discourage low-quality outreach.
